title: gulf stocks end mixed us iran tensions linger 2026 09 06
text:
Sept 6 (Reuters) - Gulf stock markets ended mixed on Sunday, with traders treading carefully ​against the backdrop of an escalating standoff ‌between Washington and Tehran.
Iran has pledged to counter crippling U.S. sanctions while threatening a "painful response" to any ​further aggression. Six months after initial U.S.-Israeli ​strikes, the conflict remains at a stalemate ⁠as diplomatic peace efforts stall following the ​collapse of a June ceasefire.
Meanwhile, tit-for-tat military action ​has resumed after a brief July lull, with U.S. Central Command confirming it struck three Iranian tankers ​on Saturday in retaliation for ballistic missile ​attacks on two U.S. Navy warships.
